meaning.en: To keep a straight, unsmiling face.
meaning.zh: 板着脸，不露笑容。

examples.zh: 他整天绷着脸，谁也不敢跟他说话。
examples.en: He keeps a stern face all day and nobody dares speak to him.

examples.zh: 她绷着脸，其实心里在偷笑。
examples.en: She kept a straight face while secretly laughing.

usage.en: Note běng (to stretch tight). 板着脸 is a very close alternative.
usage.zh: “绷”读 běng；近义“板着脸”。

meaning.en: To act or speak in a simple-minded, silly way.
meaning.zh: 说话做事显得傻乎乎的。

examples.zh: 你别冒傻气了，那样做不现实。
examples.en: Stop being silly; that's not realistic.

examples.zh: 他一冒傻气，大家都笑了。
examples.en: When he acted daft, everyone laughed.

usage.en: Casual, often affectionate. Northern colloquial.
usage.zh: 口语，常带亲昵调侃，北方话。

meaning.en: A careless, forgetful, slapdash person.
meaning.zh: 指粗心大意、做事马虎的人。

examples.zh: 他是个马大哈，经常忘带钥匙。
examples.en: He's a scatterbrain who often forgets his keys.

examples.zh: 别让马大哈来管账。
examples.en: Don't let a careless sort look after the accounts.

usage.en: Popularised in the 1950s by a satirical comic dialogue; 马大哈 became a stock word for a careless person.
usage.zh: 20世纪50年代经相声作品传开，成为粗心人的代称。

meaning.en: A reckless, impulsive young person who acts without thinking.
meaning.zh: 指做事莽撞、不顾后果的年轻人。

examples.zh: 他年轻时是个愣头青，常闯祸。
examples.en: As a youngster he was a rash one who often caused trouble.

examples.zh: 别学那个愣头青，遇事先想想。
examples.en: Don't copy that rash lad; think before you act.

usage.en: Describes a person; 青 hints at a green, inexperienced person.
usage.zh: 指人，“青”暗示年轻没经验。

meaning.en: Someone who throws their weight around at home but is meek outside.
meaning.zh: 指在家里逞凶、在外面却胆小怯懦的人。

equivalents: be a bully only at home
big man at home, mouse outside

examples.zh: 他在外面唯唯诺诺，回家就窝里横。
examples.en: He is meek outside but plays the tyrant at home.

examples.zh: 你这窝里横的毛病得改改。
examples.en: You've got to cure this habit of bullying only at home.

usage.en: 横 is read hèng (unreasonable, fierce), not héng.
usage.zh: “横”读 hèng，意为蛮横。

meaning.en: A person who believes everything and is easily talked round.
meaning.zh: 指没有主见、听别人几句话就相信的人。

examples.zh: 他是软耳朵，谁说什么都信。
examples.en: He's easily led and believes whatever anyone says.

examples.zh: 别做软耳朵，要有自己的判断。
examples.en: Don't be gullible; form your own judgement.

usage.en: In some regions it means 'henpecked' (耳朵软).
usage.zh: 在一些地区也指怕老婆。

natural: let the cat out of the bag

meaning.en: To let the truth slip out, exposing one's secret.
meaning.zh: 把内情或真相无意中暴露出来。

equivalents: let the cat out of the bag

examples.zh: 他一不留神就露底了。
examples.en: He carelessly gave the game away.

examples.zh: 这个计划千万不能露底。
examples.en: This plan must not leak at all.

usage.en: Often 露了底; here 露 is lòu (colloquial).
usage.zh: 常说“露了底”，“露”读 lòu。

meaning.en: To be rebuffed and humiliated when asking for something.
meaning.zh: 比喻求人或办事遭到拒绝，很难堪。

examples.zh: 他去求人帮忙，碰了一鼻子灰。
examples.en: He went for help and was turned away.

examples.zh: 他不听劝，结果碰一鼻子灰。
examples.en: He wouldn't listen and was snubbed.

usage.en: Usually 碰了一鼻子灰; compare 碰钉子.
usage.zh: 常说“碰了一鼻子灰”，近“碰钉子”。

meaning.en: To leave things to chance in the hope of a lucky break.
meaning.zh: 碰运气，指凭运气行事。

examples.zh: 复习都没复习，他就想撞大运。
examples.en: He hasn't revised at all and just hopes to get lucky.

examples.zh: 创业不能靠撞大运。
examples.en: You can't start a business by relying on luck.

usage.en: Often 撞撞大运; can be playful or critical.
usage.zh: 常说“撞撞大运”，可调侃，也可批评。

meaning.en: To seize a place and act as its master; to carve out one's own fiefdom.
meaning.zh: 原指强盗占据山寨称王，比喻独霸一方、自立山头。

examples.zh: 公司里有人占山为王，各自为政。
examples.en: Some people in the company carve out fiefdoms and go their own ways.

examples.zh: 他在这个部门占山为王多年。
examples.en: He has ruled this department like a little king for years.

usage.en: Originally bandits holding a mountain stronghold, as in classic novels.
usage.zh: 本指山寨强盗，见于古典小说，现多指搞山头主义。

meaning.en: To use personal connections to get something done.
meaning.zh: 通过熟人或关系办事。

examples.zh: 他托关系给孩子找了份工作。
examples.en: He pulled strings to find his child a job.

examples.zh: 办这件事得托点关系。
examples.en: You'll need some connections for this.

usage.en: Mildly negative, as it suggests favouritism.
usage.zh: 暗含走后门之意，略带贬义。

meaning.en: To get someone with influence to put in a good word.
meaning.zh: 请有面子的人帮忙说情或办事。

equivalents: get someone to put in a word

examples.zh: 她托人情才让孩子进了这所学校。
examples.en: She called in a favour to get her child into this school.

examples.zh: 这事得托个人情。
examples.en: You'll have to call in a favour for this one.

usage.en: Close to 托关系, but stresses the favour owed (人情).
usage.zh: 与“托关系”相近，强调人情。

meaning.en: To embarrass oneself by being snubbed.
meaning.zh: 自找没趣，遭到冷遇而难堪。

examples.zh: 他去搭讪，反倒讨了个没趣。
examples.en: He tried chatting her up and just got snubbed.

examples.zh: 别去讨没趣了。
examples.en: Don't go and embarrass yourself.

usage.en: Usually 讨了个没趣; sometimes 自讨没趣.
usage.zh: 常说“自讨没趣”“讨了个没趣”。

meaning.en: To warn people of a danger so they take care.
meaning.zh: 比喻提醒人们警惕危险。

examples.zh: 这起事故给大家敲响了警钟。
examples.en: This accident has sounded the alarm for everyone.

examples.zh: 专家再次敲警钟，提醒大家注意健康。
examples.en: Experts again sounded the alarm, urging people to watch their health.

usage.en: Very common in news; usually 敲响警钟.
usage.zh: 新闻中很常见，常说“敲响警钟”。

meaning.en: To stop or warn against something; to block a request.
meaning.zh: 比喻发出警告、禁止通行或不予批准。

examples.zh: 这个项目在审批时被亮了红灯。
examples.en: The project was given a red light during approval.

examples.zh: 健康指标亮红灯，必须注意休息。
examples.en: His health indicators are flashing red; he must rest.

usage.en: Modern; opposite 开绿灯.
usage.zh: 现代说法，反义“开绿灯”。

natural: back someone up from the sidelines

meaning.en: To help someone's case indirectly by chiming in from the side.
meaning.zh: 比喻在一旁帮腔、从侧面协助。

examples.zh: 你去说，我在旁边给你打边鼓。
examples.en: You do the talking; I'll back you up from the side.

examples.zh: 他在会上打边鼓，帮朋友说话。
examples.en: At the meeting he chimed in to help his friend.

usage.en: From opera, where the side drum accompanies the main players. 敲边鼓 is equally common.
usage.zh: 源自戏曲，边鼓为主演伴奏。“敲边鼓”同样常用。

meaning.en: To seize on someone's fault or slip to use against them.
meaning.zh: 比喻抓住别人的把柄或缺点。

examples.zh: 别让对手抓辫子。
examples.en: Don't let your rival get something on you.

examples.zh: 他处处小心，生怕被人抓辫子。
examples.en: He is careful all round, afraid someone will catch him out.

usage.en: 揪辫子 and 抓小辫子 are common alternatives; the 辫子 is the 'handle' by which one is held.
usage.zh: “揪辫子”“抓小辫子”同样常用，辫子比喻把柄。

natural: be gossiped about behind one's back

meaning.en: To criticise or slander someone behind their back.
meaning.zh: 在背后指责、议论别人。

examples.zh: 做这种事，不怕被人戳脊梁骨吗？
examples.en: Doing this, aren't you afraid of being talked about behind your back?

examples.zh: 他生怕别人戳他的脊梁骨。
examples.en: He's scared people will gossip behind his back.

usage.en: Usually passive: 被人戳脊梁骨. Splits: 戳他的脊梁骨.
usage.zh: 常用被动式“被人戳脊梁骨”。

meaning.en: To ruin the good name of a shop or brand.
meaning.zh: 比喻把名声、信誉搞坏。

examples.zh: 偷工减料会砸了自家的牌子。
examples.en: Cutting corners will wreck your own brand.

examples.zh: 不能为了赚钱而砸牌子。
examples.en: You can't ruin the name just to make money.

usage.en: The 牌子 is the shop's signboard, standing for its reputation. Opposite: building a name (创牌子).
usage.zh: “牌子”即店铺招牌，代表信誉；反义为“创牌子”。

meaning.en: To unload one's grievances and sufferings on someone.
meaning.zh: 向人诉说心中的委屈和苦楚。

examples.zh: 她一见朋友就倒苦水。
examples.en: She pours out her woes the moment she sees a friend.

examples.zh: 他向我倒了一晚上的苦水。
examples.en: He poured his troubles on me all evening.

usage.en: 倒 is dào (to pour). Close to 诉苦.
usage.zh: “倒”读 dào，近“诉苦”。

meaning.en: To study and gain an education.
meaning.zh: 指读书受教育。

examples.zh: 他在国外喝了几年墨水，学到不少东西。
examples.en: He drank in a few years of learning abroad and picked up a lot.

examples.zh: 年轻人多喝点墨水，才有出息。
examples.en: Young people must soak up more learning to get ahead.

usage.en: Often 肚子里有墨水 (well-read) or 没喝过墨水 (uneducated). Slightly humorous.
usage.zh: 常说“肚子里有墨水”，带幽默。

meaning.en: To tease someone's curiosity or desire without satisfying it.
meaning.zh: 故意引起别人的兴趣或欲望而不满足。

examples.zh: 他话说一半，故意吊大家的胃口。
examples.en: He said half and deliberately kept everyone in suspense.

examples.zh: 预告片只是吊吊观众的胃口。
examples.en: The trailer only whets the audience's appetite.

usage.en: Usually 吊人胃口 or 吊足胃口.
usage.zh: 常说“吊人胃口”“吊足胃口”。

meaning.en: To quibble over exact words rather than the real meaning.
meaning.zh: 在个别字词上过分斤斤计较。

examples.zh: 不要抠字眼，我的意思你明白。
examples.en: Don't nitpick the wording; you know what I mean.

examples.zh: 他喜欢抠字眼，没完没了。
examples.en: He loves to quibble over words endlessly.

usage.en: Compare 咬文嚼字, which is more neutral (weighing words carefully).
usage.zh: “咬文嚼字”较中性，指对用词推敲。

meaning.en: To put on airs or feign reluctance to raise one's value.
meaning.zh: 故意装腔作势、摆出不情愿的样子。

examples.zh: 请他吃饭，他还拿起乔来了。
examples.en: I invited him to dinner and he started playing hard to get.

examples.zh: 你别再拿乔了，大家都等着呢。
examples.en: Stop making a show of it; everyone's waiting.

usage.en: Usually 拿乔 / 拿起乔来. Close to 拿架子, but stresses feigned reluctance.
usage.zh: 与“拿架子”近，侧重故意推托。

meaning.en: To get conceited after a bit of success.
meaning.zh: 比喻有一点成绩就骄傲自满。

examples.zh: 刚得了奖，他就开始翘尾巴了。
examples.en: He had hardly won a prize before he turned cocky.

examples.zh: 成绩再好也不能翘尾巴。
examples.en: However good your results, don't get cocky.

usage.en: Often 夹着尾巴 is the opposite (keep a low profile).
usage.zh: 反义常为“夹着尾巴做人”。
